format_decision.reason: The project has too many planning markdown files for reliable orchestration. This file captures versions, dependencies, gates, active work, and a rolling planning frontier as structured data for Roadmap Lens and PlanRuntime.

planning_model.intent: The roadmap must stay at least one useful step ahead of active execution. It is not a static snapshot and not an unbounded speculative graph.

tree_layers.meaning: Nodes that can be claimed or are currently running.
Nodes that are ready to promote when current execution finishes or blocks.
Likely next branches with enough metadata for planning, but not yet claimable.
Ideas, domain tracks, and research branches that remain visually connected but muted.

agents_must_not: promote speculative nodes to claimable work without policy approval
create infinite planning branches to avoid execution

frontier_rules: Every active leaf should have at least one prepared_next node unless it is intentionally terminal.
A prepared_next node must include role, scope, gates, expected evidence, and stop rules.
Frontier candidates may be broader, but must state the uncertainty that keeps them unclaimable.
When a node completes, PlanRuntime promotes the best prepared_next child and asks for frontier refresh.
When a node blocks, PlanRuntime creates or activates an unblocker/gate node instead of skipping ahead.
When two branches touch the same hot file or capability, PlanRuntime adds a collision edge and blocks parallel claims.
If the graph grows without execution progress, the heartbeat must stop and ask for pruning or priority confirmation.

critical_risks.risk: Planning becomes self-referential and agents keep expanding the tree instead of shipping.
critical_risks.mitigation: Limit frontier depth and require execution progress or explicit operator approval before broadening.

critical_risks.risk: Agents mutate the roadmap to make their own work look unblocked.
critical_risks.mitigation: Use append-only plan events and distinguish proposed, accepted, and committed graph state.

critical_risks.risk: Speculative future branches become visually indistinguishable from approved work.
critical_risks.mitigation: Render candidate/speculative nodes muted and make claimability a separate explicit field.

critical_risks.risk: Collision and gate data becomes decorative rather than enforced.
critical_risks.mitigation: PlanRuntime must use collision/gate edges in assignment and dispatch decisions.

tomorrow_parallel_start.goal: Start several agents in parallel without write collisions. Each agent reads a scoped slice, returns a structured report, and the PlanGraph reducer decides which reports become accepted events.
tomorrow_parallel_start.operator_intent: Today is roadmap shaping only. Tomorrow should begin with maximum safe parallelism and no direct file writes from worker agents until the report protocol and claimability are clear.

launch_sequence.name: orchestrator_bootstrap
launch_sequence.action: Load this roadmap, verify git status, identify current untracked roadmap files, and open a report-ingest queue.
launch_sequence.exit: Known worktree state and ready-to-dispatch read-only scout packets.

launch_sequence.name: parallel_read_only_scouts
launch_sequence.action: Dispatch read-only agents for roadmap inventory, runtime model audit, report schema design, Lens graph design, and gate/collision policy.
launch_sequence.exit: All scouts submit AgentReport payloads only.

launch_sequence.name: plan_graph_reduction
launch_sequence.action: Validate reports, reject unsafe/raw reports, reduce accepted reports into plan events and prepared_next nodes.
launch_sequence.exit: Claimable implementation slices are explicit and collision-aware.

launch_sequence.name: implementation_wave_decision
launch_sequence.action: Choose whether to start write-capable implementation or continue read-only refinement.

parallel_scout_packets.task: Classify current roadmap files into active, done, deferred, speculative, stale, and candidate-for-import groups.
Map existing models to the new rolling roadmap, report protocol, and PlanRuntime needs.
Design the first AgentReport schema and report-to-plan-event reducer using existing handoff and truth models where possible.
must_not: let reports directly mutate graph state
treat report success as verified done

parallel_scout_packets.task: Report how Roadmap Lens v1 should visualize rolling tree layers, versions, gates, collisions, active nodes, and prepared_next nodes.
must_not: hide gates or collisions as decorative edges

parallel_scout_packets.task: Report the first enforceable collision, gate, stop, and claimability rules for read-only and later write-capable agents.

acceptance_for_tomorrow_start: Every scout has a read_scope, report_focus, and must_not list.
No scout is write-capable in the first wave.
All reports go through PlanGraph ingest before becoming future context.
Parallelism is blocked on any shared write request, live execution request, or raw-private-content report.

AUTO1-AUTO8 provide models and fake/injected planning, but real thread/git/test hooks remain open.

Defines registered agents, work items, file locks, budgets, and assignment decisions.
Provides memory/event-log durability and performance-gate evidence for future capsules.
Defines safe derived RAPTOR write gates and bounded graph-memory evidence.
Defines derived-only read-through cache and invalidation evidence.

Useful as a later multiagent benchmark for triage, duplicate detection, and field mapping.

Useful as a later scoped-write worker benchmark.

version_horizons.label: Now
version_horizons.description: Convert roadmap sprawl into structured runtime state and reconcile completed fake-runtime work.
First real multiagent foundation: structured PlanRuntime, claims, capsules, real gate runners, and read-only Roadmap Lens.

version_horizons.label: After 0.9
version_horizons.description: Live execution backend, thread bridge integration, heartbeat dispatch, worktree isolation, and dashboard operations.

version_horizons.label: Later / Research
version_horizons.description: Visual agent programming and domain-specific worker tracks after the core runtime is trustworthy.

graph_nodes.title: Reconcile markdown roadmaps into structured PlanRuntime seed
graph_nodes.objective: Create a canonical structured plan from current roadmap files, marking AUTO/SUB fake-foundation work as done and current/future tracks as active or deferred.
graph_nodes.why: The current planning state is spread across many markdown files and recent untracked roadmap drafts. Multiagent orchestration needs one structured state before dispatch can be trusted.

evidence_summary: Alice and Bob read-only scout reports reduced into structured context.
Feature pushed to fuzzy/dev and installed through the homeserver auto-updater.
Live /api/version, app health, and Chroma heartbeat checks passed.

deliverables: Dependency graph for next implementation plan
blocked_actions: Do not rewrite existing roadmap markdown as the source of truth.
Do not start live subagent execution from reconciliation alone.

graph_nodes.title: Define rolling frontier and plan mutation policy
graph_nodes.objective: Make the roadmap a living tree that always keeps one prepared step ahead while preventing runaway planning and silent gate bypasses.
graph_nodes.why: A static roadmap snapshot will become stale as soon as agents complete, block, or discover collisions. The tree needs controlled mutation rules before agents navigate it.

evidence_summary: Rolling frontier policy now requires live feature evidence before done.
After live-verified completion, the orchestrator must select the next claimable node by dependencies, gate/collision/lock clearance, and priority_rank.
If no unambiguous node is claimable, the orchestrator must record the blocking gate or stop reason instead of inventing work.
Read-only reports may propose nodes or events but cannot make nodes claimable without accepted reducer/orchestrator policy.

deliverables: Live completion and next-claim selection rule
blocked_actions: Do not let agents silently promote their own speculative nodes.
Do not allow planning expansion to replace execution progress.

graph_nodes.title: Define read-only agent report protocol
graph_nodes.objective: Let agents inspect assigned scope read-only and submit structured reports to the PlanGraph instead of mutating plan state directly.
graph_nodes.why: This creates a safe first multiagent mode: agents can gather context, detect blockers, propose next nodes, and attach evidence without changing files or self-approving progress.
deliverables: Context compiler rules for future agents
blocked_actions: Do not let read-only reports directly mark nodes done.
Do not persist raw chat logs or raw private source content as future context.
Do not treat agent observations as truth until the PlanGraph accepts the derived event.

graph_nodes.title: Build PlanRuntime as the source of truth
graph_nodes.objective: Move from roadmap text to structured PlanGraph, slices, dependencies, horizons, gates, evidence, and status transitions.
graph_nodes.why: Subagents need deterministic work items, not prose. Markdown should be rendered from structured plan state.
deliverables: Derived markdown renderer later, not first
blocked_actions: No free-form roadmap status writes without a structured event.

graph_nodes.title: Bind SubagentRuntime to PlanRuntime slices
graph_nodes.objective: Require every durable subagent run to originate from a PlanRuntime node and scoped ContextCapsule.
graph_nodes.why: The fake subagent foundation exists; the missing trust boundary is making plan/capsule/run mandatory for worker execution.
blocked_actions: No durable worker from natural-language prompt alone.

graph_nodes.title: Implement slice claims, leases, file locks, and budgets
graph_nodes.objective: Make multiagent coordination explicit before running multiple write-capable workers.
graph_nodes.why: AUTO8 already models agent pools and locks. The next step is making those decisions persistent and enforceable.
blocked_actions: Do not auto-clear locks without a gate.
Do not create unknown agents to satisfy capacity.

graph_nodes.title: Roadmap Lens v1 read-only graph
graph_nodes.objective: Show roadmap files, structured plan nodes, milestones, dependencies, active work, deferred work, gates, and hotspots in the existing Lens graph style.
graph_nodes.why: The operator loses overview when many plan files exist. A versioned graph makes current, 0.9, after-0.9, and later work visible at once.
deliverables: Nodes for roadmaps, slices, versions, gates, agents, commits, and files
Edges for depends_on, references, supersedes, active_run, touches_file, produces_evidence
Visual horizon bands: Now, 0.9, After 0.9, Later
blocked_actions: Do not allow visual edits in v1.
Do not infer completion from markdown wording without evidence.

graph_nodes.title: Turn quality gates into real scoped runners
graph_nodes.objective: Evaluate git, tests, evidence, scope, hotfiles, and handoff with real local checks where safe.
graph_nodes.why: Current runtime quality gates mostly evaluate injected snapshots. verified_done needs observed evidence.
blocked_actions: No destructive git operations.
No broad shell command runner.

graph_nodes.title: Add real execution backend behind SubagentExecutionBackend
graph_nodes.objective: Keep FakeSubagentExecutionBackend for tests and add a real backend adapter behind the same spawn/read/cancel/retry/status contract.
graph_nodes.why: Subagent Runtime v1 is fake-only by design. A real backend is the boundary between simulated and real multiagent execution.
blocked_actions: No live thread execution by default.
No raw provider or private thread content in evidence.

graph_nodes.title: Make Thread Lifecycle Bridge read and route real threads
graph_nodes.objective: Read thread state, map it to AgentRuns, detect new turns and handoffs, and block ambiguity.
graph_nodes.why: The bridge currently validates assignments and references; live multiagent work needs observed thread lifecycle state.
blocked_actions: No blind sends into unknown or ambiguous threads.

graph_nodes.title: Run the Heartbeat Runtime Loop against real state
graph_nodes.objective: Use PlanRuntime, claims, thread state, handoff mailbox, and gates to dispatch next safe work.
graph_nodes.why: The current loop plans ticks from injected snapshots. Real multiagent work requires safe dispatch, wait, resolve, and stop decisions.
blocked_actions: No endless autonomous loop without visible stop criteria.

graph_nodes.title: Give write-capable workers isolated branches or worktrees
graph_nodes.objective: Prevent simultaneous write workers from corrupting one worktree and make integration explicit.
graph_nodes.why: File locks help, but real parallel implementation needs separate patch surfaces.
blocked_actions: No shared dirty write tree for parallel implementation workers.

graph_nodes.title: Build orchestration dashboard control center
graph_nodes.objective: Show active plans, subagents, claims, leases, gates, handoffs, commits, blockers, and next actions.
graph_nodes.why: Multiagent state must be visible without reading many chat histories.
blocked_actions: No destructive controls in dashboard v1.

graph_nodes.title: Integrate Memory/RAPTOR into scoped ContextCapsules
graph_nodes.objective: Use durable memory and derived graph state as bounded capsule input, not global chat dumps.
graph_nodes.why: Memory durability and RAPTOR foundations exist. Multiagent runs need relevant project memory, decisions, and prior evidence with strict redaction.
blocked_actions: No global memory dump into subagent prompts.

graph_nodes.title: Use domain roadmaps as multiagent end-to-end benchmarks
graph_nodes.objective: Validate the runtime with realistic workflows: GitHub issue triage, Telegram operator channel, Nextcloud inbox, and GameDev write work.
graph_nodes.why: Domain tracks should test the core runtime after it is trustworthy, not fork their own orchestration logic.
blocked_actions: Do not let domain tracks bypass PlanRuntime, claims, gates, or capsules.

graph_nodes.title: Telegram rich text rendering
graph_nodes.objective: Convert assistant Markdown into Telegram-safe rich HTML or safe fallback plaintext without exposing tokens, chat IDs, or raw rich payloads.
graph_nodes.why: Telegram currently surfaces raw Markdown-like text. Rich text must be safe and tested before draft streaming is enabled.
deliverables: Redacted status fields for formatting mode
blocked_actions: Do not send live Telegram messages without explicit operator Go.
Do not persist bot tokens, raw chat IDs, sender IDs, or raw rich payloads.
Do not enable draft streaming before rich text validation is green.

graph_nodes.title: Telegram rich message draft streaming
graph_nodes.objective: Add gated Telegram rich-message draft previews for long-running agent turns, followed by idempotent final rich-message delivery or safe fallback.
graph_nodes.why: Long-running agent work needs operator-visible progress, but streaming must not create duplicate messages, leak sensitive payloads, or bypass final delivery guarantees.
deliverables: Final rich message sender with fallback
Fake Telegram provider tests and optional operator-gated live smoke
blocked_actions: Do not broaden Telegram turns with shell or arbitrary file-write tools.
Do not treat draft delivery as final answer persistence.
Do not run live Telegram sends without explicit operator Go.

graph_nodes.title: Visual agent programming in Roadmap Lens
graph_nodes.objective: Allow the operator to visually create slices, connect dependencies, assign agents, attach gates, and start runs.
graph_nodes.why: This is the long-term interface for planning and steering agents, but it should only come after read-only Lens and runtime gates are reliable.
blocked_actions: No visual mutation before PlanRuntime validation exists.
No direct graph-to-live-run without explicit operator action.

plan_event_model.reason: A mutating roadmap needs an audit trail. Current graph state should be derived from accepted events, not overwritten prose.

event_types.effect: Stores a redacted structured observation report as untrusted input.
Records that schema, scope, redaction, and source provenance passed validation.
Records why a report could not affect future context or plan state.
Allows derived plan events, gates, context summaries, or frontier proposals to be generated from the report.
Adds a candidate node that is not claimable yet.
Promotes a proposed node into the committed graph.
Moves a prepared node into current_execution when dependencies and gates allow it.
Creates or refreshes a lease for one agent.
Marks a node blocked and may propose an unblocker node.
Attaches pass, warn, block, fail, or skip evidence to a node or edge.
Adds a collision edge between nodes, files, capabilities, or agents.
Marks verified completion only after required evidence and gates pass.
Adds or updates prepared_next and frontier_candidates after progress.
Keeps a branch visible but removes claimability.

read_only_agent_report_pipeline.goal: Keep agents read-only at first. They inspect scoped context, then send a structured report to the PlanGraph. The PlanGraph validates, redacts, reduces, and only then updates future context.
future_context_rules: Future agents receive accepted report summaries and derived events, not raw report bodies by default.
Every context item must carry source_refs and confidence.
Rejected reports remain audit-only and must not be used as factual context.
Conflicting reports create a gate or blocker instead of silently choosing one.
A report may propose a next node, but cannot make that node claimable.
critical_limits: Read-only agents can still pollute context with confident but wrong summaries.
The PlanGraph reducer must preserve uncertainty instead of smoothing it away.
Reports must be compact; large raw notes, logs, provider output, and chat dumps are not valid context artifacts.

selection_order: Read current_execution nodes assigned to the agent role.
Filter out nodes with unsatisfied dependencies.
Filter out nodes with active collision, lock, or required gate blockers.
Prefer nodes with explicit ContextCapsule and focused tests.
After live-verified completion, select the next claimable node by dependency satisfaction, gate/collision/lock clearance, and priority_rank.
If no current node is claimable, inspect prepared_next and request promotion.
If prepared_next is empty for an active leaf, propose a frontier refresh instead of inventing work.
If multiple nodes are equally claimable and overlap risk is unclear, stop for orchestrator choice.
must_stop_when: the next node is not claimable
a required gate is block or fail
a file or capability collision exists
the agent lacks role, budget, lease, or workspace permission
the node would require live execution without operator Go
the agent would need to mutate the graph to make its own work valid

visual_rules: Show Now and 0.9 nodes as primary.
Show After 0.9 nodes behind the 0.9 milestone band.
Show Later/Research nodes muted and farther back.
Show current_execution, prepared_next, frontier_candidates, and speculative_backlog as separate visual layers inside each version band.
Highlight claimable nodes separately from candidate nodes.
Render collision edges as blocking edges, not decorative references.
Render gate nodes and stop conditions on the path an agent would traverse.
Warn when a markdown roadmap is newer than this JSON artifact.
Render done fake-runtime work as foundation, not as active work.
Show when a branch needs frontier refresh because no prepared_next node exists.
